section_summary: This section covers SCAP regulation of Japanese fishing and whaling in 1949, including a new fisheries inspection system, limits on expansion of the authorized fishing area, and approval of the 1949–50 Antarctic whaling expedition. It also documents protests over Chinese seizures of Japanese fishing vessels and an account of the sinking of the Akashi-maru No. 105. Related material includes production forecasts, requests for fisheries publications, whaling reports, and newspaper clippings.

subfiles.title: Notice to Allied missions of proposed Japanese fishery inspection system
subfiles.to: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan and other Far Eastern Commission missions
subfiles.about: Notifies Allied missions that SCAP intends to authorize unarmed Japanese fisheries inspection vessels.
subfiles.summary: Announces the proposed inspection system and encloses the contemplated instruction to Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fish Production and Distribution
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ press release on Japanese fish production and distribution.
subfiles.summary: Highlights projected catches, improving supplies, and changes to fish transport and marketing.

subfiles.title: Overall Fisheries Production
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Projects Japanese catches and describes improvements in fisheries supplies, handling, transport, inspection, and research.
subfiles.summary: Forecasts increased catches through 1951 as material shortages ease. Describes added ice and cold storage, rail refrigeration, fish grading, sanitation, and research on declining sardine and herring fisheries.

subfiles.title: Expansion of Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Korean concern over expansion of Japan’s authorized fishing area and SCAP’s conditions for any expansion.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a press clipping, conversation memorandum, SCAP policy statement, diplomatic note, and Japanese industry clipping. SCAP says expansion depends on compliance, conservation, and discussion with directly concerned nations.

subfiles.title: Fisheries Still Bound by MacArthur Line
subfiles.from: United Press, Pacific Stars and Stripes
subfiles.about: Reports that GHQ denied a Japanese petition to expand fishing grounds.
subfiles.summary: Says Japanese fishermen must satisfy occupation conditions before boundary relaxation.

subfiles.title: Protest by Korean Government Against Westward Extension of MacArthur Line
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Records Ambassador Chung’s objections to possible Japanese fishing-area expansion toward Korea.
subfiles.summary: Chung cites competition, security, and violations of the existing line, and seeks Korean arrest powers. Huston says no westward extension is under consideration and explains SCAP’s position on policing Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Fishing Areas
subfiles.about: States conditions for considering expansion of the Japanese fishing area.
subfiles.summary: Requires regulatory compliance, sustained-yield management, and consultation with interested nations.

subfiles.title: Reply to Korean Diplomatic Mission on Japanese fishing-area expansion
subfiles.about: Assures Korea that SCAP will not expand Japan’s fishing area before specified conditions and consultations.
subfiles.summary: Confirms rejection of Japan’s recent petition and promises discussion with directly concerned nations.

subfiles.title: Fishing Industry to Revamp Setup
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed readjustment of western-seas dragnet and trawl fishing after SCAP rejected expansion.
subfiles.summary: The ministry proposes a 30 percent industry readjustment and stricter compliance with existing limits.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of letter to T. Chawanya
subfiles.from: Stillman Wright, Fish and Wildlife Service
subfiles.to: W. M. Chapman, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a reply to a Japanese newspaper manager seeking fisheries publications.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the outgoing reply and copies of the correspondence.

subfiles.title: Reply to T. Chawanya about fisheries publications
subfiles.about: Directs Chawanya to SCAP’s Fisheries Division for approval of a publications request.
subfiles.summary: Offers available publications if SCAP forwards an approved, more specific request.

subfiles.title: Request for marine products industry publications
subfiles.about: Requests pamphlets and materials to support a marine products industry newspaper.
subfiles.summary: Chawanya describes his Hakodate newspaper and asks for fisheries materials.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Directive Authorizing Japanese Fishery Inspection System
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 1033/2 and a press release about the Japanese fishery inspection fleet.
subfiles.summary: Notes the operating area, ten-mile coastal restriction, absence of police powers, and eleven planned vessels.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fishery Inspection System
subfiles.about: Authorizes a Japanese fisheries inspection system under detailed operating restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Defines inspection duties and a geographic operating area. Vessels must stay ten miles from foreign coasts, receive voyage authorization, avoid fishing, and have no police powers; the authorization does not settle jurisdiction or fishing rights.

subfiles.title: Inspection Service for Fishing Fleet
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces SCAP approval of Japan’s eleven-vessel fishing inspection service.
subfiles.summary: Explains radio surveillance, identification, limits on inspection vessels, and proposed penalties for fishing violations. The same release continues with unrelated notices about visiting pharmacists and educators.

subfiles.title: Transmission of 1948–49 Antarctic whaling reports
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Oslo
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding two Japanese Antarctic whaling reports to the International Bureau of Whaling Statistics.
subfiles.summary: Encloses reports on Nisshin Maru No. 1 and Hashidate Maru.

subfiles.title: Transmission of 1949 Bonin Islands whaling report
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Oslo
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding a report on Japanese whaling near the Bonin Islands.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the 1949-season report for the International Bureau of Whaling Statistics.

subfiles.title: U.S. Will Re-enter the Whaling Industry
subfiles.about: Reports Olympic Whaling Company’s preparations for a United States-flag Antarctic expedition.
subfiles.summary: Describes planned investment in a factory ship and twelve catchers, expected capacity, and Norwegian concern about competition under catch limits. Adjacent weather and shipping columns appear on the clipping.

subfiles.title: Directive Authorizing Japanese 1949–50 Antarctic Whaling Expedition
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP’s authorization for two Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes operating controls and vessel surveys, and notes limited distribution of the directive.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling Operations in the Antarctic in the 1949–1950 Season
subfiles.about: Authorizes two Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets subject to approval, reporting, routing, fuel, and vessel-survey requirements.
subfiles.summary: Requires a fleet plan, approved substitutions, ship logs, route notices, daily radio reports, and verified catch and cargo information. Liquid-cargo vessels must be surveyed; the authorization creates no precedent for later whaling seasons.

subfiles.title: Plan to Use U.S. Navy to Enforce Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.about: Discusses a planned Seventh Task Fleet patrol against seizures of Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Notes Chinese and Soviet seizures and diplomatic concerns about a naval patrol.

subfiles.title: Seizures of Japanese Fishing Vessels by Chinese Patrols
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese seizures, SCAP protests, and options for protecting Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Sebald recounts China’s claimed authority and several protests seeking release of vessels and crews. He describes reports that captured trawlers were put to military use, doubts Japanese inspection craft can stop seizures, and warns that a United States Navy patrol could create wider incidents.

subfiles.title: Chinese Mission memorandum on Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Explains and defends China’s executive order for seizing Japanese vessels beyond authorized fishing limits.
subfiles.summary: The Mission cites repeated violations, traditional fishing interests, and a draft Far Eastern Commission policy as support for Chinese enforcement.

subfiles.title: SCAP protest against Chinese seizures of Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Rejects China’s asserted authority to seize Japanese fishing vessels on the high seas.
subfiles.summary: SCAP argues that the cited Far Eastern Commission paper was unapproved and that only the Supreme Commander may enforce Japanese high-seas fishing directives. It demands an end to seizures, return of vessels and crews, and incident reports for any Japanese prosecutions.

subfiles.title: Protest concerning seizure of four Nitto Maru vessels
subfiles.about: Protests the reported capture and military use of four Japanese fishing boats.
subfiles.summary: Reports their seizure by the Chinese destroyer Chang Chih and requests their return with crews and a full account of each incident.

subfiles.title: Further protest over seven Japanese vessels seized by Chinese patrols
subfiles.about: Identifies seven additional seized Japanese vessels and renews SCAP’s protest.
subfiles.summary: Requests an end to seizures, return of vessels and crews, and full incident reports.

subfiles.title: Sebald Protests Nationalist Grab of Fishing Boats
subfiles.about: Reports Sebald’s protest over eleven seized Japanese boats and concern about their military use.
subfiles.summary: Quotes SCAP officials on the seizures, the decision to keep Japanese inspection craft unarmed, and reports of a separate fatal sinking.

subfiles.title: Sinking of Japanese Fishing Vessel by Chinese
subfiles.about: Transmits an interview memorandum and diplomatic communication concerning the sinking of Akashi-maru No. 105.
subfiles.summary: Reports that an armed Chinese vessel seized and sank the trawler on June 10, leaving four survivors; the incident was raised with the Chinese Mission.

subfiles.title: Capture and Sinking of the Akashi-maru No. 105
subfiles.about: Records Chief Engineer T. Ohata’s account of the capture, shelling, and sinking of Akashi-maru No. 105.
subfiles.summary: Ohata describes the trawler’s movements, an encounter with an armed vessel whose crew spoke Chinese, towing, shellfire, and machine-gun fire. Four survivors were rescued and repatriated; the crew casualty list begins on page 95 and continues beyond this section.
